title: Dave Canales: 'The energy was right' coming out of the bye week
headline: Moton, Wharton and Etienne practiced in full pads off IR with a decision on Sunday pending; Coker looked great at practice; Waller's role is expected to grow.
summary: Canales said the first practice after the bye was spirited but not clean, with Taylor Moton, Tershawn Wharton and Trevor Etienne back on the field after being on IR. All three got a significant number of reps in a padded, physical practice, and the team will wait to see how they respond before making any decisions on Sunday; the full injury report comes tomorrow. Michael Jackson was placed on IR with a shoulder injury that needs surgery, so he is out for the season, while his knee issue is non-surgical. Canales praised Bryce Young's ability to throw from different platforms and said the RPO game worked against Detroit because the Lions kept linebackers in the box, with Chuba Hubbard's downhill, decisive running a good fit for those concepts. He said Darren Waller has been a mismatch against linebackers and safeties, that there is still more to unlock, and that his presence helps 12 personnel and opens space for others. Jalen Coker looked great and had a nice day, but he is on a high practice load coming off quad and ankle injuries, and his status will be clarified tomorrow. Canales also praised rookie Zakee Wheatley's tackling and hands, and said he is always talking with the GM about possible roster moves ahead of the trade deadline. The Panthers play Philadelphia in Week 6.

injuries.detail: Back at practice off IR with a significant number of reps in a padded practice; Sunday availability depends on how he responds, with the injury report due tomorrow.

signals.claim: Waller's role in the passing game will expand, with more ways to use him beyond what he has done so far.
signals.note: He is third on the team in receiving yards and tied for the lead in receiving touchdowns, and the coach says there is more to come, which supports his TE fantasy value.

signals.claim: The RPO game will remain a part of the offense, with Young throwing accurately from varied platforms whenever the defense gives the space.
signals.note: His accuracy off-platform and RPO reads support his fantasy outlook, though the coach said RPOs depend on how the defense plays them.

signals.claim: Hubbard's downhill, decisive running style makes him a good fit for the RPO concepts the team uses.
signals.note: He benefits when defenses leave voids in the RPO game, which helps his rushing efficiency.
signals.quote: He's aggressive. He's downhill decisive. So it's a good combo.

signals.note: He looked good in practice, but he is managing quad and ankle issues, so check the injury report before setting lineups.

signals.claim: Etienne may or may not be ready for Sunday depending on how his body responds to the padded practice.
signals.note: He is returning from IR and looked good, but his activation is not confirmed, so his role is uncertain.

signals.claim: Wheatley is a safety-turned-defender with receiver background who may be used on special teams as a receiver, though the coach was non-committal.
signals.note: He is more of an IDP/dynasty note; the coach praised his hands and said the next step is making plays on the ball.

topics.detail: The team practiced in pads on Tuesday after the bye, with Wednesday off and a high-mileage Thursday to follow, then the normal routine.
Canales said he talks with the GM all the time about possible moves ahead of the trade deadline but would not discuss specific positions.
Wharton brings a different style from Derrick Brown, Bobby Brown and Lee Hunter, with quickness and leverage at the line of scrimmage, and is disruptive against both the run and the pass.
Canales starts his weekly prep by watching the TV broadcast of the opponent, here the Eagles, to get a feel for their story and confidence.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos’ crowd noise: ‘It’s been fantastic’
headline: Payton gave no injury or depth-chart news on a short week before Thursday's home game vs. Seattle; he did praise the running game's late consistency and said Bo Nix is still working on risk and aggression.
summary: Payton opened by noting a short week with two days of work, so installation will lean on walk-throughs and material the team has already practiced. He called Seattle's defense complete in every area, citing its front, coverage fits, run defense out of seven-and-a-half-man fronts, and pressure package, and he praised Mike Macdonald. He said the Broncos should expect a physical game against the defending Super Bowl champions and declined to share game-plan keys. On Bo Nix, he said they are trying to find cleaner first- and second-progression throws that lower the risk, while still allowing scrambling plays. He said he doesn't want to over-coach the position on game day, and that a balance of aggression and caution is the goal. He said the running game was more consistent late Sunday and that the team was able to get enough touches to find a rhythm. He added that Denver has been hit with a lot of pressure on third down, and that it will keep coming until they show they can beat it. He also called the home crowd noise fantastic, praised Sam Darnold's fit and improvement in Seattle, and spoke about the value of takeaways, including a punch-out by Talanoa Hufanga.

signals.claim: Offense will try to build more first- or second-read throws to cut Nix's risk-taking, while he keeps making off-script plays.
signals.note: The coaching staff is trying to tighten Nix's decision-making against a strong Seattle pressure defense, so his turnover risk and aggressiveness are worth watching.
signals.quote: we're constantly grinding to come to calm it down and, and, and create some matchups

signals.note: Payton cited Hufanga's early-game punch-out as a purposeful, momentum-swinging takeaway, which is a plus for his IDP value.
signals.quote: It happened with Huff early in the game last week.

topics.detail: The Broncos have two days of work before Thursday. Payton said they will lean on walk-throughs and previously practiced material, and he's glad the game is at home.
Payton called Seattle's defense complete, with a good front, strong coverage fits, a good run defense and a good pressure package. He credited Mike Macdonald for building it quickly.
Payton said the run game had more consistency late in Sunday's game and that a rhythm requires enough touches. He did not name a specific back or discuss roles.
Payton acknowledged that Denver has faced heavy pressure looks on third down and said teams will keep sending it until the offense proves it can beat it.
Payton called the home crowd's atmosphere fantastic and noted that the crowd quiets down when asked.

title: Sean McVay & Matthew Stafford speak on the Rams’ 37-34 Week 5 overtime loss to the Bills
headline: McVay owns a costly late-game decision after the 37-34 OT loss to Buffalo; Puka Nacua's 17-catch game shows he is the focal point of the offense, and there were no injury updates.
summary: McVay was visibly frustrated after the overtime loss, saying he was proud of the team's fight but sick over how it ended. He blamed himself for kicking a field goal on a third-and-five situation instead of calling a better play and going for it. He said the kicking game, including the early kick coverage and the field goal, cost them. He could not explain why the pre-snap penalties persisted despite a week of emphasis and said he would review the film. He said he never considered a two-point try after the late regulation touchdown. Stafford, in the same session, said the team fought hard and scored plenty in the second half, but the penalties, the crowd noise and the short week made things hard. He praised Buffalo and Josh Allen's ability to make plays with his feet. Stafford singled out Puka Nacua's 17-catch night, saying he can access all areas of the field and is excellent on screens, over the middle and on the perimeter. No injuries were discussed.

signals.claim: Nacua remains the primary target who is used on screens, over the middle and on the perimeter
signals.note: A 17-catch game and Stafford's praise reinforce Nacua as a target hog and a weekly WR1, especially on a short week.
signals.quote: he can access all areas of the field

signals.claim: Stafford said crowd noise hurt pre-snap communication on the late quick-snap touchdown and that he can do a better job of cleaning up false starts
signals.note: Pre-snap penalties and noise were a recurring problem, which could hurt offensive rhythm in loud road environments.
signals.quote: obviously loud environment. I can do a better job of cleaning that up

topics.detail: McVay took the blame for kicking a field goal rather than going for it on third-and-five, and said he did not consider a two-point try after the late regulation touchdown. Stafford said they quick-snapped near the goal line, trusting their guys when they had Buffalo reeling.
McVay could not explain why the pre-snap issues continued despite the emphasis during the week and said he would study the film. Stafford pointed to the loud environment and false starts.
McVay said the kick coverage start and the field goal were not good enough, though he felt the coverage got cleaned up and he saw some positives.
Both McVay and Stafford said they must reset quickly on a short week and avoid letting the loss beat them twice.
